start_here: Say to your AI: "Check that the files attached to these incoming messages are really in my Files before you take them in." It runs tool:check-incoming-attachments on the batch and hands it back with each attachment's real name and media type.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of its own: it only finds each attached file among the Files handed to it and fills in what it found.
instructions: 1. Gather the batch of arrivals or messages as items, each naming its attachments by their Files identity (1f: and 64 hex characters).
2. Read the person's Files this batch names from where they are kept, and hand them in as stored.files: { name: { base64 } or { text } }. A name not handed in is not there.
3. Say "Check these attachments"; the AI runs tool:check-incoming-attachments with {items, stored}.
4. Each distinct identity is found once among the files handed in; the name and media type the carrier claimed are replaced by the file's own.
5. If any identity is missing, malformed or not among the files handed in, the whole batch is refused before anything is taken in, and the message says which file.

worked_examples.title: A forged attachment name is replaced by the file's own name and type
worked_examples.ask: Check the attachment on this incoming message before keeping it.
